issue_context.title: [iOS] System.Tests.PosixSignalRegistrationTests: RemoteExecutor is not supported on this platform.
issue_context.body:
A couple of tests, added recently in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/54136, fail with the following:
```
System.PlatformNotSupportedException : RemoteExecutor is not supported on this platform.]]>
   at Microsoft.DotNet.RemoteExecutor.RemoteExecutor.Invoke(MethodInfo method, String[] args, RemoteInvokeOptions options, Boolean pasteArguments)
   at Microsoft.DotNet.RemoteExecutor.RemoteExecutor.Invoke(Action`1 method, String arg, RemoteInvokeOptions options)
   at System.Tests.PosixSignalRegistrationTests.SignalHandlerCalledForRawSignals(PosixSignal s)
   at System.Reflection.RuntimeMethodInfo.Invoke(Object obj, BindingFlags invokeAttr, Binder binder, Object[] parameters, CultureInfo culture)
```

- System.Tests.PosixSignalRegistrationTests.SignalHandlerCalledForRawSignals
- System.Tests.PosixSignalRegistrationTests.SignalHandlerCalledForKnownSignals

cc @steveisok

The Unix implementation uses synchronization to ensure the handlers don't get called after `Dispose` returns.
This way it is guaranteed when the handler can no longer cancel the signal.

Do we want to add it here too? Or maybe we want to remove it from the Unix implementation?

That's a reasonable goal, and it's something that's been important for CancellationTokenRegistration.Dispose.  However, my expectation is that the predominant use case here is different, with someone registering for a signal and then either never unregistering or doing so at the end of the program, so I'm not sure how important that guarantee is.  There's also a potential for deadlock that can result, which is why CTR subsequently added an Unregister that didn't have the synchronization. 

I'll merge this and we can subsequently decide whether to add it to the Windows implementation or remove it from the Unix one.  I agree we should keep it the same across them.
